decision: Choose when clarification is worth its burden and when an answer remains unsupported.
primary_outcome: Correct resolved decisions per eligible case, jointly with necessary questions, wasted questions and unresolved outcomes.
denominator: All assigned cases; report transport failures, abstentions and invalid/repeated questions as separate categories.
independence_unit: Household or scenario family; multiple oracle states and trajectories may share the same underlying case.
quality_guardrail: Unsupported definitive answers, question burden and complete transcript/provenance coverage.
minimum_data: Case/family ID, oracle provenance, available and withheld facts, complete question/answer transcript, policy version, result and transport status.
failure_handling: Never classify transport failure as deliberate abstention. Missing historical transcripts limit conclusions and cannot be reconstructed from aggregates.
release_rule: Use deterministic replay to validate policy logic, with a separate evidence label from fresh model behavior; unresolved facts prevent definitive decisions when they can flip the answer.
reversal: Question burden rises without reducing outcome ambiguity, or a withheld fact changes the claimed definitive answer.
status: PROPOSED MEASUREMENT CONTRACT; NOT AN EXECUTED DOMAIN EXPERIMENT
defense: Only when the remaining uncertainty cannot change the decision. Fewer questions alone is not success if correctness falls.
Can replay validate historical model behavior?
No. It validates the replayed policy under known cases. It cannot establish trajectories that were never recorded.
